subject: Proposal: Modular SLA tranches + oncall escalation add-on
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@brightcart.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightcart.com
Date: Fri, 4 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA packaging — modular tranches, oncall add-on?

Hi Marcus,

Following our call this morning — thanks for the overview. We're trying to model a support approach that lets BrightCart scale quickly without overpaying in Q1/Q2 of rollout. Two asks from my side:

1) Can you send a modular SLA proposal that prices "tranches" (i.e., committing to an uptime band / throughput corridor with the option to add additional tranches as we grow)? We want clear breakpoints so we can map to forecasted consumption.

2) Oncall / escalation add-on — we'd like a priced option for 24x7 escalation for production incidents (night/weekend) that can be toggled per tranche. Also curious how uptime credits would be calculated if we have multiple tranches active.

If you can share a one-page pricing sketch + a short mutual action plan (dates for pilot -> GA -> commit), that would help procurement. We have an internal RFP timeline and hope to finalize by end of July.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of Infrastructure Programs
BrightCart

P.S. Procurement looped in this thread (procurement@brightcart.com).

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@brightcart.com>
Cc: naomi@redwood.com, sofia@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 4 Jul 2025 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA packaging — modular tranches, oncall add-on?

Hi Elena — appreciate the clarity. Attached is a compact sketch (proposed-tranche-pricing.pdf) and a draft mutual action plan (mutual-action-plan.xlsx). High-level summary below.

Key idea: tranche = committed throughput/availability corridor for a billing period. Each tranche has a base retainer (covers monitoring, SLA guarantees, and a non-exempt incident bucket). Oncall add-on is an optional retainer that expands escalation coverage and reduces response windows. Credits are applied to the tranche that experiences the violation (not across tranches), with a simple rollover mechanism if you have overlap.

Pricing sketch (monthly, illustrative):
- Tranche A (pilot): up to 50k requests/day; 99.5% monthly uptime guarantee; base retainer $4,500; incident labor billed at T&M beyond included bucket.
- Tranche B (growth): up to 200k requests/day; 99.9% uptime; base retainer $12,000.
- Tranche C (enterprise): >200k/day; 99.99% uptime; base retainer $28,000.

Oncall / escalation add-on (optional per tranche):
- 9x5 oncall (business hours rapid triage): +$750/mo per tranche
- 24x7 oncall (full escalation roster, phone routing, priority paging): +$3,500/mo per tranche
- Rapid-response onsite/white-glove (reserved blocks): priced separately as hourly blocks.

Discounts and commitments: we can offer an early-adopter tranche discount (applies to base retainer only) for an annual prepay or a 12-month commit. I'll defer specifics to Naomi (cc'd) but ballpark is 10–20% depending on TCV and payment terms.

Uptime credits / calculation:
- Credits are applied pro-rata to the tranche that missed the SLA. If multiple tranches overlap and both see impact, credits are applied independently to each.
- We support a single aggregated credit cap per calendar month (we recommend 100% of the base retainer for that tranche as a cap).

Next steps (suggested):
1) Naomi will propose firm discount levels / prepay options.
2) We update the M-A-P with milestone dates and a Docusign link.
3) If acceptable, schedule a 30-min redlines call the week of Jul 7 to run through contract items (marketplace split, data residency notes).

Attachments: proposed-tranche-pricing.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Best,
Marcus Lin
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
Marcus Lin | marcus@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@brightcart.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: sofia@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 6 Jul 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA packaging — modular tranches, oncall add-on?

Hi Elena — quick follow from procurement/finance perspective. Two pragmatic concessions we can make if BrightCart signs a 12‑month commit and prepays quarterly:

1) First-year tranche retainer discount: 20% off base retainer for the first 12 months (applies only to base retainer, not oncall add-ons or T&M).
2) Marketplace split: we can accept a 70/30 marketplace revenue share (BrightCart keeps 70%) for any usage sold via your marketplace channel for the first year. After year one we re-evaluate.

A couple of clarifications we recommend adding to the MAP and contract:
- Rollover credits: unused incident hours from a tranche's included bucket can rollover for one month only and cannot be aggregated across tranches.
- Canary fallback: we include a canary-fallback policy (automatic model/region fallback) as part of Tranche B and above; this reduces the likelihood of a tranche-level SLA breach and should be called out in the runbook.

If you want a slightly deeper commercial (e.g., 25% off for a 24-month prepay), we can run that, but that'll need executive approval. Happy to discuss on a quick call.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Director, Commercial Ops — Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com

From: Elena Morales <elena@brightcart.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightcart.com
Date: Mon, 7 Jul 2025 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA packaging — modular tranches, oncall add-on?

Marcus / Naomi — thanks, this is helpful and gets us most of the way there. A few follow-ups before procurement runs the paperwork: 

- Can you add a short worked example in the PDF showing how credits would look if Tranche B hits a 99.6% month while Tranche C remains unaffected? That will help our finance team map to revenue leakage.
- Confirm that the oncall add-on pricing would be applied per tranche independently (so if we have Tranche A + Tranche B active, and only B opts into 24x7, only B pays the add-on).
- We need a one‑line clause in the MAP that says marketplace channel fees are excluded from SLA credit calculations.

Procurement is ok with the 12-month, quarterly prepay and 20% first-year retainer discount — we'll circulate a PO after we see the worked example and a brief Docusign with those terms. Can we schedule a 30-min redlines call on Tue Jul 8 or Wed Jul 9?

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Best,
Elena
Head of Infrastructure Programs — BrightCart
